text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - USDA said private exporters reported sales of 112,000 tonnes of corn to Mexico.

SOYBEAN SALE - South Korea's state Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp bought 20,000 tonnes of U.S. No 1 soybean from Louis Dreyfus and another 20,000 tonnes from Continental Grain, an official at the corporation said.
SOYMEAL TENDER - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation said it had passed on tenders to buy 40,000 tonnes of soymeal due to higher than expected prices.

VEGOIL SALE - CCC bought a total of 1,400 tonnes U.S. vegetable oil for donation to Tajikistan. The vegoil was purchased in the range of $839.55 to $843.55 a tonne, FAS and shipment was due on August 19-September 3.

WHEAT TENDER - Jordan is scheduled to tender July 23 for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter or hard red spring wheat or equivalent wheat from other countries, U.S. exporters said. Half of the tonnage was slated for last-half August shipment and the balance for last-half September shipment.

CORN/SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said it wanted to buy 30,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine No. 2 yellow corn for arrival in the second half of September and/or the second half of October and 30,000 tonnes of soybeans, any origin, for arrival first half of October and/or first half of November. The deadline for the corn and soybean bids is noon (0900 GMT) July 22, he told Reuters.

RICE TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs will receive offers until July 23 to buy 24,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery, a GEZA spokesman said. Results would be available on July 24.
RICE TENDERS cont'd - The CCC said it was seeking on July 22 a total of 1,780 tonnes U.S. long grain rice for donation to Burkina Faso. The shipment period was due for August 21 to September 5.
MARKET TALK - Thailand is set to allow the feed industry to import an additional 150,000 tonnes of tariff-free corn for the rest of the year, a commerce ministry official said.

... Zambia will import 120,000 tonnes of the staple maize from neighbouring Zimbabwe to reduce a shortfall caused by a 32 percent drop in domestic production, the country's food reserve agency said. Zambia had only 15,000 tonnes of maize stocks left, an agency spokesman said.
... Malaysian corn prices were holding steady this week but buyers were sidelined awaiting consolidation following recent sharp corrections on the Chicago corn market, industry sources said.
